_readme: Source of truth for /publications/. Add new papers at the top of "papers" (any order works; the build script sorts them), then run: python3 scripts/build.py. Titles may contain simple HTML such as <i>, <sub>, <sup>. status = published | accepted | submitted. first_author / student_led are true/false. Links are generated from bibcode (or arxiv), arxiv and doi; add any extra links under "links".

papers.authors: A. A. Khostovan, R. L. Sanders, et al.
papers.title: The AURORA Survey: The Mass–Metallicity and Fundamental Metallicity Relations at z ∼ 2.3 Based Purely on Direct Te Metallicities
papers.summary: Direct-method (electron-temperature) oxygen abundances for 34 galaxies at z ≈ 1.4–3.5 from JWST/AURORA give a calibration-free mass–metallicity relation at cosmic noon. None of six cosmological simulations reproduces its evolution since z ≈ 2.

papers.authors: A. A. Khostovan, J. Kartaltepe, et al.
papers.title: COSMOS Spectroscopic Redshift Compilation (First Data Release): 488k Redshifts Encompassing Two Decades of Spectroscopy
papers.summary: A public compilation of 487,666 spectroscopic redshifts for 266,284 objects in COSMOS from 138 programs, with self-organizing maps identifying the galaxy populations that still lack spectroscopic coverage.

papers.authors: A. A. Khostovan, J. Kartaltepe, et al.
papers.title: EELG1002: A Record-Breaking [O III]+Hβ EW ∼ 3700 Å Galaxy at z ∼ 0.8 – Analog of Early Galaxies?
papers.summary: EELG1002, identified in archival Gemini spectra, has a record [O III]+Hβ equivalent width of 3,100–3,700 Å, 32–36 times typical for its mass and epoch, and properties closely matching reionization-era galaxies.

papers.authors: A. A. Khostovan, S. Malhotra, J. Rhoads, et al.
papers.title: Evolution of Hα Equivalent Widths from z ∼ 0.4–2.2: implications for star formation and legacy surveys with Roman and Euclid
papers.summary: Forward modeling of Hα equivalent widths at z ≈ 0.4–2.2 shows that galaxies with bursty star formation produced 40–60% of all new stars at cosmic noon, with forecasts for Roman and Euclid grism surveys.

papers.authors: A. A. Khostovan, S. Malhotra, J. Rhoads, et al.
papers.title: Correlations between Hα Equivalent Width and Galaxy Properties at z = 0.47: Physical or Selection-Driven?
papers.summary: Forward modeling of survey selection shows that the Hα equivalent width–stellar mass anticorrelation is intrinsic but shallower than observed (∝ M−0.16), and that low-mass galaxies are intrinsically burstier.

papers.authors: A. A. Khostovan, S. Malhotra, J. Rhoads, et al.
papers.title: A large, deep 3 deg² survey of Hα, [O III], and [O II] emitters from LAGER: constraining luminosity functions
papers.summary: Hα, [O III], and [O II] luminosity functions and star-formation rate densities at z = 0.47, 0.93, and 1.59 from LAGER, one of the deepest narrowband surveys to date.

papers.authors: A. A. Khostovan, D. Sobral, B. Mobasher, et al.
papers.title: The clustering of typical Lyα emitters from z ∼ 2.5–6: host halo masses depend on Lyα and UV luminosities
papers.summary: The clustering of about 5,000 Lyα emitters at z ≈ 2.5–6 reveals a redshift-independent relation between line luminosity (relative to L*) and dark matter halo mass.

papers.authors: A. A. Khostovan, D. Sobral, B. Mobasher, et al.
papers.title: The clustering of Hβ+[O III] and [O II] emitters since z ∼ 5: dependencies with line luminosity and stellar mass
papers.summary: The clustering of about 7,000 Hβ+[O III] and [O II] emitters to z ≈ 5 reveals a redshift-independent relation between line luminosity (relative to L*) and dark matter halo mass.

papers.authors: A. A. Khostovan, D. Sobral, B. Mobasher, et al.
papers.title: The nature of Hβ+[O III] and [O II] emitters to z ∼ 5 with HiZELS: stellar mass functions and the evolution of EWs
papers.summary: Stellar mass functions and equivalent-width evolution for about 7,000 Hβ+[O III] and [O II] emitters to z ≈ 5, implying higher ionization parameters in high-redshift galaxies.

papers.authors: A. A. Khostovan, D. Sobral, B. Mobasher, et al.
papers.title: Evolution of the Hβ+[O III] and [O II] Luminosity Functions and the [O II] Star-Formation History of the Universe up to z ∼ 5
papers.summary: The largest samples at the time of Hβ+[O III] and [O II] emitters to z ≈ 5, giving luminosity functions and the cosmic star-formation history from a single tracer.
